subject: english-language
title: From Coos to Words
welcome_lead: Trace the first eighteen months of language — from melodic cooing to the magical first word.
meta_desc: Pre-verbal cooing, babbling and the holophrastic stage in child language acquisition at A-Level.
final_note: You have followed the child from coo to word — each stage a rehearsal for the grammar to come.

concepts.def: 0-6 months: melodic vowel-like sounds, exploring the vocal tract.
6-12 months: reduplicated (mama, dada) and variegated babble, narrowing toward the ambient language's phonology.
12-18 months: single words function as whole utterances (milk = I want milk).
The set of distinctive sounds in a language; babbling first explores broadly then narrows to ambient inventory.
Using a word for a wider class than its adult meaning (doggy for all four-legged animals).
Using a word for a narrower class (cup only for the child's own cup).

walkthroughs.body_html:
From around 6 weeks infants produce cooing — soft vowel-like sounds linked to comfort. These are pre-linguistic but reveal vocal-tract maturation.

Caregivers respond with CDS, beginning the conversational dance.

Around 6 months, reduplicated babbling appears: mamama, baba. By 10 months variegated babbling combines different syllables.

Cross-linguistic studies show that the babble inventory narrows toward the ambient language by 12 months — children stop producing sounds not used around them.

From around 12 months single words carry whole-utterance meaning. Up can mean pick me up, I want up there, or look up.

Intonation and context disambiguate — early communication is a partnership.

mcqs.q: What is the telegraphic stage of child language development?
options: It is the stage when children first start using a telephone.
Piaget was a behaviourist who emphasised reinforcement.
Around age 2-3, children produce short utterances containing content words but omitting function words and inflections (e.g. 'mummy gone shop').
It is the stage where children memorise long stories.

mcqs.q: What did Chomsky propose about language acquisition?
options: Piaget was a behaviourist who emphasised reinforcement.
Chomsky said children learn language entirely by copying adults.
Chomsky said children should be taught grammar from age two.
Children possess an innate Language Acquisition Device — an inborn capacity for grammar — because exposure alone cannot account for how rapidly and uniformly children learn complex syntax.

mcqs.q: How does Piaget's theory relate language to cognitive development?
options: Language develops as a consequence of cognitive development — children must first develop concepts (object permanence, conservation) before they can express them linguistically. Cognition leads language.
Chomsky said children should be taught grammar from age two.
Piaget was a behaviourist who emphasised reinforcement.
Piaget said language drives cognitive development.
